Subject: NDex: post-demo recap & proposed validation plan

Alex — thanks again for your time today. Quick recap from our demo and a proposed plan so we keep momentum.

High-level pain points you called out:
- Latency spikes on bursts (p95 occasionally > 1s at 512-1024 tokens)
- Cost concerns when scaling to multi-tenant ingestion pipelines
- Need for on-prem/VPC option for PHI-sensitive workloads and auditability

Goals you confirmed:
1) Reduce per-request tail latency to <200ms p95 for typical 128-token queries; keep 512-token p95 under 400ms where possible.
2) Drive unit inference cost down by ~3x versus current setup (model + infra).
3) Validate a Private deployment path (VPC + KMS integration) with retention/audit controls.

Open questions / items we committed to answer:
- Detailed latency breakdown by model variant (we'll surface kernel-level p95s)
- Cost projection for 1M queries/month with batching & prefix caching
- SOC2 / security evidence for procurement (you mentioned procurement will ask)

Suggested next steps (proposed ecosystem PoC):
1) Mutual action plan: 2-week sandbox PoC running three baseline scenarios (low latency, high throughput, cold-start) — attachment: NDex_Mutual_Action_Plan.xlsx
2) You to share a representative sample (25k–50k items) we can use for side-by-side runs; we'll run Redwood default quantized variant + one parity model you prefer.
3) Vendor comparison matrix: we'll run identical inputs and return latency/cost/failure-rate metrics and logs for your SE team.

If the above matches, proposed meeting to kick off the PoC Wednesday 3/24 at 11:00 PT — calendar link in my next email.

Thanks — I’ll get the test-plan template and the scoring rubric over to you today.

—

Subject: Internal: NDex vendor scoring / suggested test matrix

Folks — quick internal note following the demo and Alex’s reply. I sketched a lightweight scoring rubric and a prioritized test suite so we can be surgical with the PoC resources.

Proposed scoring categories (weights in parentheses):
- Latency (p95/p99) at 128/512 tokens (40%)
- Cost per 1M tokens (including batching/caching) (25%)
- Functional parity (response fidelity on 200-shot QA subset) (20%)
- Reliability & graceful degradation (10%)
- Ops & compliance (SOC2/KMS docs, audit log fidelity) (5%)

Suggested runbook (minimal viable experiment):
1) Cold-start latency test (single-node warmup) — 1000 queries each at 128/512 tokens
2) Throughput ramp (steady-state throughput to max sustainable qps) — measure p50/p95/p99 and error rates
3) KV/prefix-cache effect — run with and without prefix cache enabled and measure delta in token cost per request
4) Failure injection — simulate one node outage and measure fallback correctness and client-observed latency spike

Open asks for SE/infra:
- Karthik, can you provision a 2-node sandbox cluster with quantized weights and disable our cross-request cache for one of the test variants?
- Lukas, can you finalize the PoC scoring sheet and the test input mapping to the sample corpus?

I’ll prepare a short internal matrix comparing Redwood vs two market alternatives (we’ll keep the names internal until we have comparative results). Will share by EOD tomorrow.

—Camila
